svg.title: A 14-month-old with 2 days of vomiting and diarrhea has an estimated 7% weight loss, dry mucous membranes, decreased tears, and capillary refill of 3 seconds.
svg.desc: A weight loss of 5-10% in an infant with dry mucous membranes, decreased tears, and a capillary refill of 2-4 seconds matches moderate dehydration; mild dehydration in infants is closer to 5% with normal mucous membranes and a refill under 2 seconds, while severe dehydration includes a refill over 4 seconds with sunken eyes and lethargy. Oral rehydration solution is tried first for mild and moderate dehydration because it is effective and less invasive than IV therapy, which is reserved for severe dehydration or when oral rehydration fails; withholding all oral intake pending cultures would worsen the child's fluid deficit unnecessarily.
